question: Is input tax credit on a bus with an approved seating capacity of 20 persons, used by a company to ferry its own employees, blocked under section 17(5)(a) of the CGST Act?
gold_answer: Yes. On this date section 17(5)(a) blocks credit on "motor vehicles and other conveyances" except when they are used for making the taxable supplies of (A) further supply of such vehicles or conveyances, (B) transportation of passengers, or (C) imparting training on driving, flying, navigating such vehicles or conveyances, or (ii) for transportation of goods. Ferrying the company's own employees is none of these, so the credit is blocked.

question: Is input tax credit on a bus with an approved seating capacity of 20 persons, used by a company to ferry its own employees, blocked under section 17(5)(a) of the CGST Act?
gold_answer: No, not under clause (a). From 1 February 2019 section 17(5)(a) covers only "motor vehicles for transportation of persons having approved seating capacity of not more than thirteen persons (including the driver)"; a bus with an approved seating capacity of 20 is outside that clause.

question: Under section 16(4) of the CGST Act, up to when can a registered person take input tax credit on an invoice for a financial year?
gold_answer: Not after the due date of furnishing of the return under section 39 for the month of September following the end of the financial year to which the invoice or debit note pertains, or furnishing of the relevant annual return, whichever is earlier.

question: Under section 16(4) of the CGST Act, up to when can a registered person take input tax credit on an invoice for a financial year?
gold_answer: Not after the thirtieth day of November following the end of the financial year to which the invoice or debit note pertains, or furnishing of the relevant annual return, whichever is earlier.

question: Can a registered person take input tax credit on an invoice of financial year 2017-18 after the due date of the return under section 39 for September 2018?
gold_answer: No. Section 16(4) bars input tax credit on an invoice or debit note after the due date of furnishing of the return under section 39 for the month of September following the end of the financial year to which it pertains (for 2017-18, September 2018), or furnishing of the relevant annual return, whichever is earlier.

question: Can a registered person take input tax credit on an invoice of financial year 2017-18 after the due date of the return under section 39 for September 2018?
gold_answer: Yes. The proviso to section 16(4), inserted by Order No. 02/2018-Central Tax dated 31 December 2018, allows input tax credit after the due date of the September 2018 return till the due date of furnishing of the return under section 39 for March 2019, for invoices (or invoices relating to debit notes) for supplies made during 2017-18 whose details the supplier uploaded under section 37(1) till the due date for furnishing those details for March 2019.

question: Can a registered person avail input tax credit on an invoice whose details the supplier has not furnished in FORM GSTR-1 or the invoice furnishing facility?
gold_answer: Yes, but limited: under rule 36(4) such credit shall not exceed 5 per cent. of the eligible credit available in respect of invoices or debit notes whose details have been furnished by the suppliers under section 37(1) in FORM GSTR-1 or using the invoice furnishing facility.

question: Can a registered person avail input tax credit on an invoice whose details the supplier has not furnished in FORM GSTR-1 or the invoice furnishing facility?
gold_answer: No. From 1 January 2022 rule 36(4) provides that no input tax credit shall be availed in respect of such invoices or debit notes unless (a) their details have been furnished by the supplier in FORM GSTR-1 or using the invoice furnishing facility and (b) they have been communicated to the registered person in FORM GSTR-2B under rule 60(7).

question: For 2021, over which months does the rule 36(4) condition apply cumulatively, and in which return is the cumulative adjustment made?
gold_answer: The condition applies cumulatively for April and May 2021, and the return in FORM GSTR-3B for the tax period May 2021 is to be furnished with the cumulative adjustment of input tax credit for those months.

question: For 2021, over which months does the rule 36(4) condition apply cumulatively, and in which return is the cumulative adjustment made?
gold_answer: The condition applies cumulatively for April, May and June 2021, and the return in FORM GSTR-3B for the tax period June 2021 or the quarter ending June 2021, as the case may be, is to be furnished with the cumulative adjustment of input tax credit for those months.

question: Does rule 89 of the CGST Rules provide for a refund application under section 77 for tax paid on a supply treated as intra-State that is later held to be inter-State?
gold_answer: No. Rule 89 as in force on this date has no such provision; it contains no sub-rule (1A).

question: Does rule 89 of the CGST Rules provide for a refund application under section 77 for tax paid on a supply treated as intra-State that is later held to be inter-State?
gold_answer: Yes. Rule 89(1A), inserted by Notification No. 35/2021-Central Tax: such a person may, before the expiry of two years from the date of payment of the tax on the inter-State supply, file an application electronically in FORM GST RFD-01 through the common portal, directly or through a Facilitation Centre notified by the Commissioner. For tax paid on inter-State supply before the sub-rule came into force, the application may be filed within two years from the date the sub-rule comes into force.

question: Is a refund application under rule 89(1) of the CGST Rules subject to the provisions of rule 10B?
gold_answer: No. On this date rule 89(1) reads "may file an application electronically in FORM GST RFD-01" without any reference to rule 10B. The words ", subject to the provisions of rule 10B," inserted by Notification No. 35/2021-Central Tax apply only from the date notified for them, 1 January 2022 (Notification No. 38/2021-Central Tax).

question: Is a refund application under rule 89(1) of the CGST Rules subject to the provisions of rule 10B?
gold_answer: Yes. From 1 January 2022 rule 89(1) provides that the applicant "may file, subject to the provisions of rule 10B, an application electronically in FORM GST RFD-01" (Notification No. 35/2021-Central Tax, brought into force by Notification No. 38/2021-Central Tax).

question: What does section 9(4) of the CGST Act provide for supplies received by a registered person from an unregistered supplier?
gold_answer: The central tax in respect of the supply of taxable goods or services or both by a supplier who is not registered, to a registered person, shall be paid by such person on reverse charge basis as the recipient, and all the provisions of the Act apply to the recipient as if he is the person liable for paying the tax.

question: What does section 9(4) of the CGST Act provide for supplies received by a registered person from an unregistered supplier?
gold_answer: The Government may, on the recommendations of the Council, by notification, specify a class of registered persons who shall, in respect of supply of specified categories of goods or services or both received from an unregistered supplier, pay the tax on reverse charge basis as the recipient; all the provisions of the Act then apply to such recipient as if he is the person liable for paying the tax.

question: What is the rate of central tax on intra-State supply of ghee?
gold_answer: 6 per cent. central tax: "Butter and other fats (i.e. ghee, butter oil, etc.) and oils derived from milk; dairy spreads (heading 0405)" is in Schedule II of Notification No. 1/2017-Central Tax (Rate).

question: What is the rate of central tax on intra-State supply of ghee?
gold_answer: 2.5 per cent. central tax: "Butter and other fats and oils derived from milk, including ghee; dairy spreads" is in Schedule I of Notification No. 9/2025-Central Tax (Rate), in force from 22 September 2025.

question: What is the rate of central tax on intra-State supply of Portland cement?
gold_answer: 14 per cent. central tax: "Portland cement, aluminous cement, slag cement, super sulphate cement and similar hydraulic cements, whether or not coloured or in the form of clinkers" is in Schedule IV of Notification No. 1/2017-Central Tax (Rate).

question: What is the rate of central tax on intra-State supply of Portland cement?

question: What is the rate of central tax on intra-State supply of tractors (other than road tractors for semi-trailers of engine capacity more than 1800 cc)?
gold_answer: 6 per cent. central tax: "Tractors (except road tractors for semi-trailers of engine capacity more than 1800 cc) (heading 8701)" is in Schedule II of Notification No. 1/2017-Central Tax (Rate).

question: What is the rate of central tax on intra-State supply of tractors (other than road tractors for semi-trailers of engine capacity more than 1800 cc)?
gold_answer: 2.5 per cent. central tax: "Tractors (except road tractors for semi-trailers of engine capacity more than 1800 cc)" is in Schedule I of Notification No. 9/2025-Central Tax (Rate), in force from 22 September 2025.

question: What is the rate of central tax on intra-State supply of air-conditioning machines?
gold_answer: 14 per cent. central tax: "Air-conditioning machines, comprising a motor-driven fan and elements for changing the temperature and humidity, including those machines in which the humidity cannot be separately regulated" is in Schedule IV of Notification No. 1/2017-Central Tax (Rate).

question: What is the rate of central tax on intra-State supply of air-conditioning machines?
gold_answer: 9 per cent. central tax: "Air-conditioning machines, comprising a motor-driven fan and elements for changing the temperature and humidity, including those machines in which the humidity cannot be separately regulated" is in Schedule II of Notification No. 9/2025-Central Tax (Rate), in force from 22 September 2025.

question: What is the rate of central tax on intra-State supply of household dish washing machines?
gold_answer: 14 per cent. central tax: "Dish washing machines, household [8422 11 00] and other [8422 19 00]" is in Schedule IV of Notification No. 1/2017-Central Tax (Rate).

question: What does rule 86B of the CGST Rules say?
gold_answer: A registered person shall not use the amount available in the electronic credit ledger to discharge liability towards output tax in excess of ninety-nine per cent. of that liability where the value of taxable supply other than exempt supply and zero-rated supply in a month exceeds fifty lakh rupees. The restriction does not apply where (a) the person or specified officers/partners paid more than one lakh rupees as income tax in each of the last two financial years; (b)/(c) the person received refunds of more than one lakh rupees of unutilised input tax credit in the preceding financial year under clause (i) or (ii) of the first proviso to section 54(3); (d) more than 1% of total output tax liability, applied cumulatively up to the month, was paid through the electronic cash ledger; (e) the person is a Government Department, a Public Sector Undertaking, a local authority or a statutory body; or (f) the person, other than a manufacturer, is exempted in respect of goods specified under rule 31D on which tax has been paid by the supplier on the basis of retail sale price. The Commissioner or an authorised officer may remove the restriction after verifications and safeguards.

question: What does section 9(3) of the CGST Act provide?
gold_answer: The Government may, on the recommendations of the Council, by notification, specify categories of supply of goods or services or both, the tax on which shall be paid on reverse charge basis by the recipient, and all the provisions of the Act apply to such recipient as if he is the person liable for paying the tax.

question: What condition does section 16(2)(aa) of the CGST Act impose for taking input tax credit?
gold_answer: The details of the invoice or debit note referred to in clause (a) must have been furnished by the supplier in the statement of outward supplies and communicated to the recipient in the manner specified under section 37.

question: What condition does section 16(2)(ba) of the CGST Act impose for taking input tax credit?
gold_answer: The details of input tax credit in respect of the supply communicated to the registered person under section 38 must not have been restricted.

question: What does section 17(5)(aa) of the CGST Act block?
gold_answer: Input tax credit on vessels and aircraft, except when they are used (i) for making the taxable supplies of (A) further supply of such vessels or aircraft, (B) transportation of passengers, (C) imparting training on navigating such vessels, or (D) imparting training on flying such aircraft; or (ii) for transportation of goods.

question: What does section 17(5)(ab) of the CGST Act say?
gold_answer: Input tax credit is not available on services of general insurance, servicing, repair and maintenance in so far as they relate to motor vehicles, vessels or aircraft referred to in clause (a) or (aa), except that it is available (i) where those motor vehicles, vessels or aircraft are used for the purposes specified in those clauses, or (ii) where received by a taxable person engaged in the manufacture of such motor vehicles, vessels or aircraft, or in the supply of general insurance services in respect of such motor vehicles, vessels or aircraft insured by him.

question: What does rule 36(4) of the CGST Rules say?
gold_answer: No input tax credit shall be availed in respect of invoices or debit notes whose details are required to be furnished under section 37(1) unless (a) their details have been furnished by the supplier in FORM GSTR-1, as amended in FORM GSTR-1A if any, or using the invoice furnishing facility, and (b) the details of input tax credit in respect of them have been communicated to the registered person in FORM GSTR-2B under rule 60(7).

question: What does section 16(4) of the CGST Act say?
gold_answer: A registered person shall not be entitled to take input tax credit in respect of any invoice or debit note for supply of goods or services or both after the due date of furnishing of the return under section 39 for the month of September following the end of the financial year to which the invoice or debit note pertains, or furnishing of the relevant annual return, whichever is earlier.

question: What does the proviso to section 16(4) of the CGST Act say?
gold_answer: A registered person is entitled to take input tax credit after the due date of the section 39 return for September 2018 till the due date of the return for March 2019, for any invoice or invoice relating to a debit note for supplies made during financial year 2017-18, the details of which the supplier uploaded under section 37(1) till the due date for furnishing those details for March 2019.

question: What does section 17(5)(a) of the CGST Act block?
gold_answer: Input tax credit on motor vehicles for transportation of persons having approved seating capacity of not more than thirteen persons (including the driver), except when they are used for making the taxable supplies of (A) further supply of such motor vehicles, (B) transportation of passengers, or (C) imparting training on driving such motor vehicles.

question: A company buys a 7-seater car for its directors' business travel. Can it take input tax credit on the car?
gold_answer: No. Section 17(5)(a) blocks credit on motor vehicles for transportation of persons with approved seating capacity of not more than thirteen persons (including the driver) unless used for further supply of such vehicles, transportation of passengers, or imparting training on driving them. Directors' travel is none of these.

question: A car dealer buys passenger cars for resale. Is input tax credit on the cars blocked under section 17(5)(a)?
gold_answer: No. Section 17(5)(a) excepts motor vehicles used for making the taxable supply of further supply of such motor vehicles.

question: A driving school buys a hatchback car to train learner drivers. Is input tax credit on the car blocked under section 17(5)(a)?
gold_answer: No. Section 17(5)(a) excepts motor vehicles used for making the taxable supply of imparting training on driving such motor vehicles.

question: An airline buys an aircraft that it uses to operate passenger flights. Is input tax credit on the aircraft blocked under section 17(5)?
gold_answer: No. Section 17(5)(aa) blocks credit on vessels and aircraft except when used for making the taxable supply of transportation of passengers, among other exceptions; passenger flights fall within that exception.

question: A company pays for servicing and repair of a 7-seater car used for its directors' travel. Can it take input tax credit on these services?
gold_answer: No. Section 17(5)(ab) blocks credit on servicing, repair and maintenance relating to motor vehicles referred to in clause (a). The proviso allows it only where the vehicle is used for the purposes specified in clause (a), or where the recipient manufactures such vehicles or supplies general insurance for vehicles insured by it; none applies.

question: A general insurance company insures motor cars. Is input tax credit available on general insurance services relating to the cars it insures?
gold_answer: Yes. The proviso to section 17(5)(ab) makes credit on such services available where received by a taxable person engaged in the supply of general insurance services in respect of such motor vehicles insured by him.

question: The supplier did not report an invoice in FORM GSTR-1 and it does not appear in the recipient's FORM GSTR-2B. Can the recipient take input tax credit on it?
gold_answer: No. Section 16(2)(aa) requires the invoice details to have been furnished by the supplier in the statement of outward supplies and communicated to the recipient under section 37, and rule 36(4) bars credit unless the details of the invoice were furnished by the supplier in FORM GSTR-1 (or the invoice furnishing facility) and communicated to the registered person in FORM GSTR-2B under rule 60(7).

question: The input tax credit communicated to a registered person under section 38 for a supply has been restricted. Can the person take that credit?
gold_answer: No. Section 16(2)(ba) makes it a condition that the details of input tax credit in respect of the supply communicated under section 38 have not been restricted.

question: A registered person buys goods from an unregistered supplier. Must the registered person pay tax on reverse charge?
gold_answer: Only if notified. Under section 9(4) the recipient pays tax on reverse charge where the Government, on the Council's recommendations, has by notification specified a class of registered persons and categories of goods or services received from unregistered suppliers; the section by itself does not make every such purchase liable.
